title: Context windows and long-context failure: room is not attention
summary: What a context window holds and what it costs (quadratic prefill, a growing key-value cache, memory-bound decode, sparse attention's indexer), and why models fail inside the window: length alone hurting even with perfect retrieval or masked filler, softmax dilution, attention sinks, cache compression across turns, fixed-state copying limits, and tests beyond the needle.

topics: deep dive: context windows and long-context failure
concepts_taught: what a context window holds and costs: everything shares it (instructions, history, documents, tool results, the output), quadratic prefill attention, a linearly growing KV cache, memory-bound decode; NVIDIA's measurement of dense attention at 91% of per-layer prefill time at 128K

trained sparse attention as indexer + top-k (typically a few thousand keys) + core attention: the full scan moves into the indexer (47% vs 24% core attention on DeepSeek V3.2 at 128K prefill), cost follows keys scored not keys kept, and an unread token can neither confuse nor help

context length alone hurting performance despite perfect retrieval (Du et al. 2025: 13.9-85% drops across 5 models, persisting with whitespace filler, masked filler, and evidence placed before the question), with recite-the-evidence-first as the mitigation (up to 4% for GPT-4o on RULER)

attention sinks (StreamingLLM): softmax must put weight somewhere, so models park it on initial tokens; evicting them breaks sliding-window streaming; stable to 4M+ tokens but the window and memory are unchanged

long-context failure beyond retrieval: softmax dilution (Scalable-Softmax), sub-O(n) KV-cache methods failing across multi-turn shared contexts (SCBench), fixed-state models' copying limit (Repeat After Me), latent-state and multi-round coreference tests (Michelangelo's fall-off before 32K, MRCR), and output length bounded by SFT data (LongWriter)
